limitations: The beach orientation, prevailing wind, flood elevation, legal setbacks and shoreline position are assumed rather than surveyed; validate these before siting the estate.
Hurricane-resistance, corrosion specifications, structural uplift design, drainage, pool engineering, landscape planting and exterior lighting require specialist design.
The plan establishes architectural accommodation and envelope only; bespoke interiors, furniture, kitchens, bathrooms, AV, security and detailed service infrastructure remain to be developed.

plan.thesis: A low, deeply shaded Caribbean estate organized as a sequence from a limestone arrival court through a tall ocean-facing great hall to a broad covered veranda and pool. A single high living pavilion is the civic heart; quieter sleeping, guest and service wings step down behind and beside it, creating privacy without competing with the sea-facing silhouette.

masses.role: primary double-height ocean-facing living pavilion with entertaining rooms and sheltered veranda
secondary private family suite wing, reached across the covered arrival court
secondary guest accommodation and library wing
subordinate discreet service and staff wing

spaces.use: Double-height principal salon with framed southward sea view, natural light and cross-ventilation through shaded openings.
Chef's kitchen with direct service and outdoor-kitchen connection.
Formal dining room opening toward the veranda and sea.
Back kitchen, cold storage and catering preparation.
Guest powder room off the entertaining sequence.
Deep roofed outdoor living and dining veranda facing the water.
Roofed outdoor kitchen and bar, directly served from the indoor kitchen and veranda.
Roofed open-air arrival court and sheltered threshold between landward arrival and the private wing.
Private daylit gallery connecting the family suites and arrival court.
Secluded primary bedroom with filtered garden light.
Primary suite dressing room.
Primary bathroom with a screened private exterior wall.
Family bedroom suite with morning garden light.
Ensuite bathroom for family bedroom one.
Family bedroom suite with a more secluded corner outlook.
Ensuite bathroom for family bedroom two.
Quiet guest circulation gallery with framed landscape light.
Ocean-oriented guest bedroom suite.
Ensuite bathroom for guest bedroom one.
Garden-oriented guest bedroom suite set apart from the first guest room.
Ensuite bathroom for guest bedroom two.
Intimate library and retreat with shaded east light.
Discreet service entry and internal service distribution.
Laundry and linen handling room.
Staff bedroom with natural light.
Bathroom for staff accommodation.

constraints.reason: The principal living room must open directly onto its shaded sea-facing entertaining edge.
Family and guest accommodation remain acoustically and visually distinct.
The veranda should feel protected by the main house while remaining open to the sea.
